flows.representativeInput: payload/.joycraft/references/testing-review.md:7-44 at 8382a23; walk on a temp project with a fixed sleep, self-comparison, mock-supplied oracle, CI-keyed worker cap, nested runner, wall-clock flake and pbkdf2 global setup
flows.expected: Measure first runs the full suite once through evidence.mjs and reports run facts (load, cores); Find ranks by what every run pays, then the slowest file, and lists a CI-keyed control and a nested test runner.

observations.actual: Scan: testing-review.md:9-15 evidence.mjs run --receipt command, wallMs/load/cores/loaded, like-load rule; 19-20 rank by what every run pays first, then slowest file; 28-30 CI-keyed control re-keyed on JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE; 31-33 nested test runner; 38-39 no real oracle (self-comparison, subject-computed expected, mock-supplied behavior). Walk: following the text, one full run through the payload evidence.mjs printed facts {wallMs 1790, load [6.0,6.0], cores 14, loaded false}; the receipt shows runner concurrency=14 (CI=1), i.e. the CI-keyed local cap of 2 is off for agents, as the text predicts; a focused one-file run costs 218 ms with the global pbkdf2 setup vs 62 ms without, so ranking by what every run pays puts setup.mjs above the slowest file (the 1.5 s sleep); scans found the sleep, the CI control, the nested runner and both oracle defects. Tests 20/20 pass, exit 0.

limits: The flaky wall-clock test passed both full runs; the text gives no probe that surfaces it (see follow-up f1).

flows.expected: Apply writes each approved change as a test-only spec (#test-only-specs) for the queue; a deletion names the claim and the owner yes; suite time before and after; the review itself edits no test.

observations.actual: Lines 62-68: "The review itself edits no test", test-only spec link to #test-only-specs (heading exists at 109), decompose format with ## Test changes class, one file or subsystem per spec, seam/fix first, deletion names the claim, the new owner test or claim retired, and the owner yes, full-suite time and run facts before and after the queue. Line 5 unattended rule unchanged. Walk: after measure and find, git diff --quiet against the base exit 0 and the tree is clean. Mapping the walk findings: sleep and flake fixes are class 2, the self-comparison and mock oracle fixes are class 2 or a class-3 deletion, the nested test moved to a tooling suite leaves the gate (class 3, line 102-103), the CI-keyed config is shared tooling (serial lane, line 80-82).

limits: The walk drafted no specs into a real queue; the Apply mapping is a reading of the text, not a run of decompose.

flows.expected: artifacts.md, where decision options are written, offers a time limit or a result cache only after a measurement.

observations.actual: artifacts.md:55-56 sits after the consequential-choice order (42-54) and before **Words.**: an option adding a time limit or result cache is offered only after a measurement, its example gives the measured time, load or repeat count. testing-review.md:54-56 repeats it with the repeat-count measure. [AC:spec-21-3] passes.

flows.expected: payload-guard passes; every-spec words grow by at most 8; on-demand within budget.

observations.actual: All 20 pass, exit 0. Guard prints every-spec 12166 (cap 12256, 90 spare), equal to the pre-spec count 12166 (+0); on-demand 20049 (cap 21163, 1114 spare). Both edited files are on-demand.

limits: Toy-project walk on node:test only; no real field suite; the walk used the payload evidence.mjs because the installed .joycraft/runtime copy is older.

findings.summary: f1 (playbook 3.4.8): a flaky test is listed but nothing finds one. In the walk the wall-clock test passed both full runs. Add the cheap probe: one shuffled run, and one run at half the workers while another broad run is active.
findings.assumption: Not a stated criterion; closest to the brief intent of SOTA cleanup.

findings.summary: f2 (playbook 3.2): before/after is one sample each. Add: time each suspect file alone, and repeat baseline and candidate in alternating order (ABAB), at least 3 times each, at a like load, before claiming a speed-up.

f3 (playbook 3.5): a deletion ledger row lacks the break-the-code receipt for the test that now owns the claim, and the keep categories (auth, permissions, persistence, migrations, security, external formats, release) needing an owner yes per batch are absent.
f4 (playbook 3.1): no "stop the bleeding" step: install the worker cap (lane-cap, keyed on JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE) before any speed measurement; the text only notes the load.

f5: the measure command has no --timeout-ms; evidence.mjs defaults to 300000 ms, so a slow suite (the case this review exists for) times out and reports no full timing. Name --timeout-ms for the full run.

f6: "A test-only spec changes tests, fixtures and test lists only" does not name runner config or global test setup, yet lines 80-82 put runner-config changes in the test-only lane and the walk CI-key and pbkdf2 fixes are of that kind. Say runner config and test setup count, and which class (no assertion change) they take.

f7 (playbook 3.4.6, 3.6): smaller gaps: duplicate contract and debugging-probe tests not in the junk rubric; the speed refactor omits "the kept real case must kill the glue mutants" and "check a shrunk input original value as data"; before/after omits the always-on cost.

f8: like text-fault-proof and text-lane-cap, the test pins EVERY_SPEC_BEFORE=12166 and a 12-file guard list, so the next spec that adds over 8 every-spec words or changes the list turns it red (a frozen-baseline check of the kind this review text tells projects to retire). Test changes says none while a new test file is added; the spec Tests line requires it, so not blocking.
